summary.tldr: Creates a bargaining system for digital news platforms and news businesses, with CRTC oversight, exemptions, penalties, and annual reporting.
what_it_does: Applies to digital news intermediaries when there is a major bargaining power gap between the platform operator and news businesses, and lets Cabinet set rules for how that test is applied.
Creates a bargaining process so digital news intermediary operators and news businesses can make agreements about news content made available in Canada.
Requires the CRTC to keep a list of covered digital news intermediaries, set a code of conduct for bargaining, and manage a process for news businesses to join the system.
Lets the CRTC exempt a platform if it has agreements with news businesses that meet set criteria, and lets Cabinet add rules for those exemptions.
Bars operators from unfairly discriminating against certain news content or giving unjust preference or disadvantage, and lets news businesses complain to the CRTC.
Allows the CRTC to order information, impose administrative monetary penalties, recover some administration costs, and require an annual audit report on the law’s impact.
